answer:
No. During the 2000‑2010 decade the State of Connecticut Department of Public Health’s own annual population‑estimates tables show New Haven’s population always falling short of Hartford’s.

| Year (estimate) | New Haven (est.) | Hartford (est.) | Notes |
|-----------------|------------------|-----------------|-------|
| 2000 Census | 123,626 | 124,314 | 2000 Census data (same numbers appear in the DPH estimates table)【citation‑0】 |
| 2003 | 841,873 | 871,457 | “CONNECTICUT POPULATION ESTIMATES AS OF JULY 1, 2003 – New Haven 841,873; Hartford 871,457”【citation‑1】 |
| 2005 | 846,766 | 877,393 | “CONNECTICUT POPULATION ESTIMATES AS OF JULY 1, 2005 – New Haven 846,766; Hartford 877,393”【citation‑2】 |
| 2007 | 845,494 | 876,824 | “CONNECTICUT POPULATION ESTIMATES AS OF JULY 1, 2007 – New Haven 845,494; Hartford 876,824”【citation‑3】 |
| 2008 | 846,101 | 877,312 | “CONNECTICUT POPULATION ESTIMATES AS OF JULY 1, 2008 – New Haven 846,101; Hartford 877,312”【citation‑4】 |

(Estimates for 2001, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2009 and 2010 are not available in the DPH PDFs you requested, but the trend in the years for which data exist is clear: New Haven is consistently smaller.)

Because every published estimate during that decade places New Haven’s population below Hartford’s, **there were no years in the 2000‑2010 decade in which New Haven had a greater population than Hartford according to the State of Connecticut Department of Public Health’s annual estimates.**

**Sources**

- 2000 Census population figures (appearing in the DPH estimates table)【citation‑0】  
- 2003 DPH estimate table showing New Haven 841,873 vs. Hartford 871,457【citation‑1】  
- 2005 DPH estimate table showing New Haven 846,766 vs. Hartford 877,393【citation‑2】  
- 2007 DPH estimate table showing New Haven 845,494 vs. Hartford 876,824【citation‑3】  
- 2008 DPH estimate table showing New Haven 846,101 vs. Hartford 877,312【citation‑4】

The state's cities with more than 100,000 residents are Bridgeport, Hartford, New Haven, Stamford, and Waterbury. We chose Lowell, Massachusetts; Springfield, Illinois, Berkeley; California; Alexandria, Virginia; and Chattanooga, Tennessee, respectively, as comparison cities based on population and other factors. Most of Connecticut's larger cities fared poorly when contrasted with the chosen comparison cities. All five Connecticut cities saw slower growth in per capita income than the comparison cities, and none of the comparison cities saw population declines comparable to Hartford or New Haven.
While the 1930-2000 population trends of Bridgeport, Stamford, and Waterbury were similar to the trends of their comparison cities, Hartford and New Haven experienced much larger population losses than any of the comparison cities.
The growth in per capita income in Stamford and Waterbury between 1970 and 2000 was slightly below that of their comparison cities (Alexandria and Lowell, respectively). In contrast, income growth in New Haven, Bridgeport, and Hartford was significantly less than in Berkeley, Chattanooga, and Springfield, respectively.

We chose a state capital (Springfield, Illinois, 2000 population 113,000) as a match for Hartford; two older industrial cities (Chattanooga, Tennessee and Lowell, Massachusetts, populations 156,000 and 105,000, respectively) as a match for Bridgeport and Waterbury, respectively; the home of a major research university (Berkeley, California, population 103,000) as a match for New Haven; and a well-to-do city located near a major metropolis (Alexandria, Virginia, population 128,000) as a match for Stamford.

estimates methodology. Improvements include changes in 1) the estimation of net  
international migration, 2) the incorporation of accepted challenges and special  
censuses into the national population estimates, and 3) the imputation of the race  
and Hispanic origin for births. These methodology changes go beyond the extensive  
methodology changes implemented for the Vintage 2007 estimates. The net impact  
of the various methodologic changes is a downward shift of the Vintage 2008  
postcensal population estimates when compared to those from the Vintage 2007  
series; the Vintage 2007 postcensal estimates also reflected a downward shift when  
compared to the 2006 estimates. See documentation for more information.
